heard: Our universe is 13.8 billion years old, but 93 billion light years wide. Since nothing outruns light, that cosmic sphere should logically measure under 28 billion light years across. When the oldest detectable glow was emitted 380,000 years after the Big Bang, its source sat just 42 million light years away. Yet as those ancient photons spent 13.8 billion years journeying toward Earth, the distance multiplied between us. Albert Einstein proved no physical object can move locally through space faster than light. But the fabric of space itself has no speed limit, stretching relentlessly between receding galaxies. That ancient matter was carried 46 billion light years away, while its original glow was still in transit. Cosmic expansion simply stretched the distance far faster than photons could fly.
